# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain s157 (`%12`, 2026-09-09 11:09 → 11:58 AEST — the guards seat, and the one that refused a merge its coordinator had ruled) | **TWO STOPS AND A CATCH, ALL CORRECT: it refused an unapproved merge on a rule it found in the repo's own CLAUDE.md, then measured the merge that replaced it and found it had gone to the WRONG BRANCH — and it shipped KS-926 in between.** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **STOP 1 — the expensive one.** Wednesday ruled #914's merge on Kam's week-scoped grant plus a passed tier-1 gate. **s157 refused**, citing `Blockchain/CLAUDE.md` 225/226/246 — *"no approval → no merge"*, and *"a rule we keep, not one GitHub enforces — nothing technical stopped #731 being self-merged unapproved."* **Two instruments, and it volunteered its own evidence's weakness before being asked** (a shadow-flagged approval is invisible to both) **then gave the discriminator that survives it**: no `review_requested` at all. Its framing, adopted: *"that is a question about what Kam's grant covers, and it is not mine to answer by merging."* **Nothing technical would have refused that merge. The agent was the only thing between a ruled merge and a broken convention.** **STOP 2** — on Kam's ruling it attempted the approval and hit **HTTP 422 *"Can not approve your own pull request"*** (kksecura opened both PRs and is our PAT), **stopped rather than reaching for `--admin`**, and reported the exact refusal. **THE CATCH — and it is the one that saved Peter and Stuart being told a falsehood:** after Kam merged by hand, it measured six things and found **#915 had merged into #914's BRANCH, sixteen seconds after that branch was merged away from.** Both PRs `merged:true`, real merge commits, correct timestamps. Its formulation, adopted fleet-wide: ***"a PR merged into a branch that had already been merged away from, which reads as success on every instrument except ancestry."*** **The decisive instrument was not ancestry but READING THE PINS OUT OF THE LOCKFILES** — still `9.0.3`/`1.11.0`, an artefact read rather than an inference. **And it carried a positive control on the whole diagnosis**: its own branch, based on the bump, passed 14/14 in the same minute — proving the block was the missing bump and not a repo condition. **FINAL VERIFICATION after Kam's third merge: all three instruments green AND AGREEING** — ancestry (control still discriminating), both audit legs EXIT=1 → EXIT=0 with 0 unbaselined, reported count 41 → 36 *"exactly the five the bump removes"* as an internal consistency check, and the pins read from develop's lockfiles. **It named the residual honestly rather than hedging:** it measured legs 6 and 7, so a fresh worktree still meets leg 1 DEPS MISSING — an environment condition, not a repo block. **DELIVERED IN BETWEEN: KS-926, 14 of 17 guards wired with 3 deliberately not and the census, `ed954f09e`, preflight 14/14, three push refusals each diagnosed (incl. KS-1034, GIT_DIR in hooks, fixed as a CLASS), no `--no-verify` at any point.** Filed KS-1028/29/30/31/32/33/34. |
| Secuura/Blockchain s158 (`%13`, 2026-09-09 11:09 → 11:40 AEST — the systemTest half of the first two-seat parallel run) | **BOTH items to READY FOR QA, PR #916 on origin with 13/13 preflight — and a PRECONDITION Wednesday set turned out to change the design rather than merely confirm it.** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **Verified independently by Wednesday:** `584b12ba1eed99583ec60141c41dce524c926dfe` at `refs/heads/kamilkreiser/ks-993-systemtest-typecheck-entrypoint` via `ls-remote`, with a positive control (develop present) and a negative control (bogus ref, 0 li

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.
